passages.text: Then the Pharisees and some of the scribes who had come from Jerusalem gathered around Jesus, and they saw some of His disciples eating with hands that were defiled—that is, unwashed.
passages.sermon:
The Pharisees came to Jesus.
Some scribes also came to Jesus.
These scribes had come from Jerusalem.
The Pharisees and scribes gathered around Jesus.
They saw some of Jesus’ disciples.
These disciples were eating bread.
The disciples ate with hands that were defiled.
Their hands were unwashed.
passages.original: Καὶ συνάγονται πρὸς αὐτὸν οἱ Φαρισαῖοι καί τινες τῶν γραμματέων ἐλθόντες ἀπὸ Ἱεροσολύμων καὶ ἰδόντες τινὰς τῶν μαθητῶν αὐτοῦ ὅτι κοιναῖς χερσίν τοῦτ’ ἔστιν ἀνίπτοις ἐσθίουσιν τοὺς ἄρτους

passages.text: Now in holding to the tradition of the elders, the Pharisees and all the Jews do not eat until they wash their hands ceremonially.
passages.sermon:
The Pharisees follow the tradition of the elders.
All the Jews also follow this tradition.
They do not eat until they wash their hands in a special way.
They wash their hands to keep the tradition.
passages.original: Οἱ γὰρ Φαρισαῖοι καὶ πάντες οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι ἐὰν μὴ πυγμῇ νίψωνται τὰς χεῖρας οὐκ ἐσθίουσιν κρατοῦντες τὴν παράδοσιν τῶν πρεσβυτέρων

passages.text: And on returning from the market, they do not eat unless they wash. And there are many other traditions for them to observe, including the washing of cups, pitchers, kettles, and couches for dining.
passages.sermon:
The Pharisees and all the Jews follow the tradition of the elders.
They do not eat after returning from the market unless they wash themselves.
They have received many other traditions to keep.
They wash cups.
They wash pitchers.
They wash kettles.
They wash dining couches.
passages.original: καὶ ἀπ’ ἀγορᾶς ἐὰν μὴ βαπτίσωνται οὐκ ἐσθίουσιν καὶ ἄλλα πολλά ἐστιν ἃ παρέλαβον κρατεῖν βαπτισμοὺς ποτηρίων καὶ ξεστῶν καὶ χαλκίων καὶ κλινῶν

passages.text: So the Pharisees and scribes questioned Jesus: “Why do Your disciples not walk according to the tradition of the elders? Instead, they eat with defiled hands.”
passages.sermon:
The Pharisees and the scribes spoke to Jesus.
They asked Jesus a question.
They said, “Why do your disciples not follow the tradition of the elders?”
They said, “Your disciples eat bread with unwashed hands.”
passages.original: Καὶ ἐπερωτῶσιν αὐτὸν οἱ Φαρισαῖοι καὶ οἱ γραμματεῖς Διὰ τί οὐ περιπατοῦσιν οἱ μαθηταί σου κατὰ τὴν παράδοσιν τῶν πρεσβυτέρων ἀλλὰ κοιναῖς χερσὶν ἐσθίουσιν τὸν ἄρτον

passages.text: Jesus answered them, “Isaiah prophesied correctly about you hypocrites, as it is written: ‘These people honor Me with their lips, but their hearts are far from Me.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the Pharisees and scribes.
He called them hypocrites.
He said Isaiah spoke about them long ago.
Isaiah was a prophet.
Isaiah’s words are written in Scripture.
God said, “These people honor Me with their lips.”
God also said, “Their hearts are far from Me.”
passages.original: Ὁ δὲ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς Καλῶς ἐπροφήτευσεν Ἠσαΐας περὶ ὑμῶν τῶν ὑποκριτῶν ὡς γέγραπται ὅτι Οὗτος ὁ λαὸς τοῖς χείλεσίν με τιμᾷ Ἡ δὲ καρδία αὐτῶν πόρρω ἀπέχει ἀπ’ ἐμοῦ

passages.text: They worship Me in vain; they teach as doctrine the precepts of men.’
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the Pharisees and scribes.
He called them hypocrites.
He said, “These people worship Me in vain.
They teach human rules as if they are God’s commands.”
passages.original: Μάτην δὲ σέβονταί με Διδάσκοντες διδασκαλίας ἐντάλματα ἀνθρώπων

passages.text: You have disregarded the commandment of God to keep the tradition of men.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the Pharisees and scribes.
He called them hypocrites.
He said they ignored God's commandment.
They chose to keep human tradition instead.
They set aside what God commanded.
They held tightly to the rules made by people.
passages.original: Ἀφέντες τὴν ἐντολὴν τοῦ Θεοῦ κρατεῖτε τὴν παράδοσιν τῶν ἀνθρώπων

passages.text: He went on to say, “You neatly set aside the command of God to maintain your own tradition.
passages.sermon: Jesus spoke to the people.\r\nHe said, “You set aside God’s command.\r\nYou do this so you can keep your own tradition.”
passages.original: Καὶ ἔλεγεν αὐτοῖς Καλῶς ἀθετεῖτε τὴν ἐντολὴν τοῦ Θεοῦ ἵνα τὴν παράδοσιν ὑμῶν τηρήσητε

passages.text: For Moses said, ‘Honor your father and your mother’ and ‘Anyone who curses his father or mother must be put to death.’
passages.sermon:
Moses was a prophet and leader of Israel.
Moses gave God's law to the people.
Moses said, "Honor your father."
Moses said, "Honor your mother."
Moses also said, "Anyone who curses his father must be put to death."
Moses also said, "Anyone who curses his mother must be put to death."
passages.original: Μωϋσῆς γὰρ εἶπεν Τίμα τὸν πατέρα σου καὶ τὴν μητέρα σου καί Ὁ κακολογῶν πατέρα ἢ μητέρα θανάτῳ τελευτάτω

passages.text: But you say that if a man says to his father or mother, ‘Whatever you would have received from me is Corban’ (that is, a gift devoted to God), he is no longer permitted to do anything for his father or mother.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the religious leaders.
He said, "You have your own rule.
You say this:
If a man says to his father or mother, ‘Whatever help you would have received from me is Corban,’
Corban means a gift devoted to God.
Then that man is not allowed to do anything for his father or mother.
You do not let him help his parents at all."
passages.original: ὑμεῖς δὲ λέγετε Ἐὰν εἴπῃ ἄνθρωπος τῷ πατρὶ ἢ τῇ μητρί Κορβᾶν ὅ ἐστιν Δῶρον Ὃ ἐὰν ἐξ ἐμοῦ ὠφεληθῇς οὐκέτι ἀφίετε αὐτὸν οὐδὲν ποιῆσαι τῷ πατρὶ ἢ τῇ μητρί

passages.text: Thus you nullify the word of God by the tradition you have handed down. And you do so in many such matters.”
passages.sermon:
You nullify the word of God.
You do this by your tradition.
You handed down this tradition.
You do many other similar things.
passages.original: ἀκυροῦντες τὸν λόγον τοῦ Θεοῦ τῇ παραδόσει ὑμῶν ᾗ παρεδώκατε καὶ παρόμοια τοιαῦτα πολλὰ ποιεῖτε

passages.text: Once again Jesus called the crowd to Him and said, “All of you, listen to Me and understand: Nothing that enters a man from the outside can defile him; but the things that come out of a man, these are what defile him.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the people.
He called the crowd to Himself.
He said, "Listen to Me, all of you.
Understand what I say.
Nothing that comes into a person from outside can make him unclean.
Only what comes out of a person makes him unclean."
passages.original: Καὶ προσκαλεσάμενος πάλιν τὸν ὄχλον ἔλεγεν αὐτοῖς Ἀκούσατέ μου πάντες καὶ σύνετε οὐδέν ἐστιν ἔξωθεν τοῦ ἀνθρώπου εἰσπορευόμενον εἰς αὐτὸν ὃ δύναται κοινῶσαι αὐτόν ἀλλὰ τὰ ἐκ τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐκπορευόμενά ἐστιν τὰ κοινοῦντα τὸν ἄνθρωπον

passages.text: After Jesus had left the crowd and gone into the house, His disciples inquired about the parable.
passages.sermon:
Jesus left the crowd.
He went into the house.
His disciples were with Him.
The disciples asked Jesus about the parable.
passages.original: Καὶ ὅτε εἰσῆλθεν εἰς οἶκον ἀπὸ τοῦ ὄχλου ἐπηρώτων αὐτὸν οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ τὴν παραβολήν

passages.text: “Are you still so dull?” He asked. “Do you not understand? Nothing that enters a man from the outside can defile him, because it does not enter his heart, but it goes into the stomach and then is eliminated.” (Thus all foods are clean.)
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
He said, “Are you still without understanding?”
He asked, “Do you not see this?”
Nothing that enters a person from outside can make him unclean.
What enters from outside does not go into his heart.
It goes into his stomach.
Then it passes out of the body.
This means all foods are clean.
passages.original: Καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς Οὕτως καὶ ὑμεῖς ἀσύνετοί ἐστε οὐ νοεῖτε ὅτι πᾶν τὸ ἔξωθεν εἰσπορευόμενον εἰς τὸν ἄνθρωπον οὐ δύναται αὐτὸν κοινῶσαι ὅτι οὐκ εἰσπορεύεται αὐτοῦ εἰς τὴν καρδίαν ἀλλ’ εἰς τὴν κοιλίαν καὶ εἰς τὸν ἀφεδρῶνα ἐκπορεύεται καθαρίζων πάντα τὰ βρώματα

passages.text: He continued: “What comes out of a man, that is what defiles him.
passages.sermon: Jesus spoke to His disciples.\r\nHe said, “What comes out of a person defiles that person.”
passages.original: Ἔλεγεν δὲ ὅτι Τὸ ἐκ τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐκπορευόμενον ἐκεῖνο κοινοῖ τὸν ἄνθρωπον

passages.text: For from within the hearts of men come evil thoughts, sexual immorality, theft, murder, adultery, greed, wickedness, deceit, debauchery, envy, slander, arrogance, and foolishness.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
He explained what truly defiles a person.
Evil comes from inside people.
Evil comes from the human heart.
Evil thoughts come from within.
Sexual immorality comes from within.
Theft comes from within.
Murder comes from within.
Adultery comes from within.
Greed comes from within.
Wickedness comes from within.
Deceit comes from within.
Debauchery comes from within.
Envy comes from within.
Slander comes from within.
Arrogance comes from within.
Foolishness comes from within.
passages.original: ἔσωθεν γὰρ ἐκ τῆς καρδίας τῶν ἀνθρώπων οἱ διαλογισμοὶ οἱ κακοὶ ἐκπορεύονται πορνεῖαι κλοπαί φόνοι μοιχεῖαι πλεονεξίαι πονηρίαι δόλος ἀσέλγεια ὀφθαλμὸς πονηρός βλασφημία ὑπερηφανία ἀφροσύνη

passages.text: All these evils come from within, and these are what defile a man.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the people.
He explained what makes a person unclean.
Evil things come from inside a person.
These evil things come from the heart.
All these evils come from within.
These evils make a person unclean.
passages.original: πάντα ταῦτα τὰ πονηρὰ ἔσωθεν ἐκπορεύεται καὶ κοινοῖ τὸν ἄνθρωπον

passages.text: Jesus left that place and went to the region of Tyre. Not wanting anyone to know He was there, He entered a house, but was unable to escape their notice.
passages.sermon:
Jesus left that place.
He went to the region of Tyre.
Jesus entered a house.
He did not want anyone to know He was there.
But people noticed Him.
He could not remain hidden.
passages.original: Ἐκεῖθεν δὲ ἀναστὰς ἀπῆλθεν εἰς τὰ ὅρια Τύρου Καὶ εἰσελθὼν εἰς οἰκίαν οὐδένα ἤθελεν γνῶναι καὶ οὐκ ἠδυνήθη λαθεῖν

passages.text: Instead, a woman whose little daughter had an unclean spirit soon heard about Jesus, and she came and fell at His feet.
passages.sermon:
Jesus entered a house in the region of Tyre.
A woman heard about Jesus.
This woman had a little daughter.
Her daughter had an unclean spirit.
The woman came to Jesus.
She fell at Jesus’ feet.
passages.original: ἀλλ’ εὐθὺς ἀκούσασα γυνὴ περὶ αὐτοῦ ἧς εἶχεν τὸ θυγάτριον αὐτῆς πνεῦμα ἀκάθαρτον ἐλθοῦσα προσέπεσεν πρὸς τοὺς πόδας αὐτοῦ

passages.text: Now she was a Greek woman of Syrophoenician origin, and she kept asking Jesus to drive the demon out of her daughter.
passages.sermon:
The woman was Greek.
She was Syrophoenician by birth.
She had a daughter with an unclean spirit.
She came to Jesus.
She kept asking Jesus to cast the demon out of her daughter.
passages.original: ἡ δὲ γυνὴ ἦν Ἑλληνίς Συροφοινίκισσα τῷ γένει καὶ ἠρώτα αὐτὸν ἵνα τὸ δαιμόνιον ἐκβάλῃ ἐκ τῆς θυγατρὸς αὐτῆς

passages.text: “First let the children have their fill,” He said. “For it is not right to take the children’s bread and toss it to the dogs.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the woman.
He said, “Let the children eat first.”
He said, “It is not right to take the children’s bread.”
He said, “It is not right to throw the bread to the dogs.”
passages.original: Καὶ ἔλεγεν αὐτῇ Ἄφες πρῶτον χορτασθῆναι τὰ τέκνα οὐ γάρ ἐστιν καλόν λαβεῖν τὸν ἄρτον τῶν τέκνων καὶ τοῖς κυναρίοις βαλεῖν

passages.text: “Yes, Lord,” she replied, “even the dogs under the table eat the children’s crumbs.”
passages.sermon:
The woman was Greek.  
She was Syrophoenician by birth.  
She spoke to Jesus.  
She said, "Yes, Lord."  
She said, "Even the dogs under the table eat the crumbs from the children."
passages.original: Ἡ δὲ ἀπεκρίθη καὶ λέγει αὐτῷ Ναί Κύριε καὶ τὰ κυνάρια ὑποκάτω τῆς τραπέζης ἐσθίουσιν ἀπὸ τῶν ψιχίων τῶν παιδίων

passages.text: Then Jesus told her, “Because of this answer, you may go. The demon has left your daughter.”
passages.sermon: Jesus spoke to the woman.\r\nHe said, “Because you gave this answer, you may go.”\r\nThe demon has left your daughter.”
passages.original: Καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῇ Διὰ τοῦτον τὸν λόγον ὕπαγε ἐξελήλυθεν ἐκ τῆς θυγατρός σου τὸ δαιμόνιον

passages.text: And she went home and found her child lying on the bed, and the demon was gone.
passages.sermon:
The woman went home.
She entered her house.
She saw her child lying on the bed.
The demon had left her child.
Her child was free from the demon.
passages.original: καὶ ἀπελθοῦσα εἰς τὸν οἶκον αὐτῆς εὗρεν τὸ παιδίον βεβλημένον ἐπὶ τὴν κλίνην καὶ τὸ δαιμόνιον ἐξεληλυθός

passages.text: Then Jesus left the region of Tyre and went through Sidon to the Sea of Galilee and into the region of the Decapolis.
passages.sermon:
Jesus left the region of Tyre.
He traveled through Sidon.
He went to the Sea of Galilee.
He entered the region of the Decapolis.
passages.original: Καὶ πάλιν ἐξελθὼν ἐκ τῶν ὁρίων Τύρου ἦλθεν διὰ Σιδῶνος εἰς τὴν θάλασσαν τῆς Γαλιλαίας ἀνὰ μέσον τῶν ὁρίων Δεκαπόλεως

passages.text: Some people brought to Him a man who was deaf and hardly able to speak, and they begged Jesus to place His hand on him.
passages.sermon:
Some people brought a man to Jesus.
This man could not hear.
This man could hardly speak.
The people begged Jesus to place His hand on the man.
passages.original: Καὶ φέρουσιν αὐτῷ κωφὸν καὶ μογιλάλον καὶ παρακαλοῦσιν αὐτὸν ἵνα ἐπιθῇ αὐτῷ τὴν χεῖρα

passages.text: So Jesus took him aside privately, away from the crowd, and put His fingers into the man’s ears. Then He spit and touched the man’s tongue.
passages.sermon:
Jesus is the Son of God.
Jesus met a man who was deaf and could hardly speak.
Jesus took the man away from the crowd.
Jesus was alone with the man.
Jesus put His fingers into the man’s ears.
Jesus spit.
Jesus touched the man’s tongue.
passages.original: Καὶ ἀπολαβόμενος αὐτὸν ἀπὸ τοῦ ὄχλου κατ’ ἰδίαν ἔβαλεν τοὺς δακτύλους αὐτοῦ εἰς τὰ ὦτα αὐτοῦ καὶ πτύσας ἥψατο τῆς γλώσσης αὐτοῦ

passages.text: And looking up to heaven, He sighed deeply and said to him, “Ephphatha!” (which means, “Be opened!”).
passages.sermon:
Jesus looked up to heaven.
He sighed deeply.
He spoke to the man.
Jesus said, “Ephphatha!”
“Ephphatha” means, “Be opened!”
passages.original: καὶ ἀναβλέψας εἰς τὸν οὐρανὸν ἐστέναξεν καὶ λέγει αὐτῷ Ἐφφαθά ὅ ἐστιν Διανοίχθητι

passages.text: Immediately the man’s ears were opened and his tongue was released, and he began to speak plainly.
passages.sermon:
Jesus healed a man who could not hear or speak.
Immediately, the man’s ears opened.
His tongue became free.
He began to speak clearly.
passages.original: καὶ ἠνοίγησαν αὐτοῦ αἱ ἀκοαί καὶ εὐθὺς ἐλύθη ὁ δεσμὸς τῆς γλώσσης αὐτοῦ καὶ ἐλάλει ὀρθῶς

passages.text: Jesus ordered them not to tell anyone. But the more He ordered them, the more widely they proclaimed it.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the people who saw the miracle.
He gave them a command.
He told them not to tell anyone about what happened.
Jesus repeated this order to them.
The people did not obey.
They talked about the miracle even more.
They spread the news widely.
passages.original: Καὶ διεστείλατο αὐτοῖς ἵνα μηδενὶ λέγωσιν ὅσον δὲ αὐτοῖς διεστέλλετο αὐτοὶ μᾶλλον περισσότερον ἐκήρυσσον

passages.text: The people were utterly astonished and said, “He has done all things well! He makes even the deaf hear and the mute speak!”
passages.sermon:
Jesus healed a man who was deaf and mute.
The people saw this miracle.
The people were completely amazed.
They said, “He has done everything well.”
They said, “He makes the deaf hear.”
They said, “He makes the mute speak.”
passages.original: καὶ ὑπερπερισσῶς ἐξεπλήσσοντο λέγοντες Καλῶς πάντα πεποίηκεν καὶ τοὺς κωφοὺς ποιεῖ ἀκούειν καὶ τοὺς ἀλάλους λαλεῖν
